column1: Purpose: Validate that full backup, incremental backup, and restore workflows remain data-correct, state-consistent, and recoverable when key control-plane, execution, storage, resource, and network dependencies are disrupted. Test descriptions are written for both engineering and project-management review.

column2: Test Title
column4: Test Objective / Description
column6: Chaos Action
column10: Expected Behavior
column12: How to Verify
column13: Expected Outcome

column2: Stop the virtual machine backup process during a full backup
column4: Verify that an in-progress full backup fails safely when the component performing the actual disk copy is stopped, without advancing the backup checkpoint or corrupting the VM state.
column5: Virtual machine launcher pod running the backup
column6: Delete the launcher pod
column7: During the active disk-copy period, after the backup has started and before it completes
column10: The backup should report a clear failure. The backup checkpoint must not advance. The VM should restart and Changed Block Tracking should return to its enabled state.
column11: Automatic VM restart; run a fresh full backup to confirm recovery.
column12: Check backup result and failure reason, confirm checkpoint did not advance, confirm VM and Changed Block Tracking recover, then perform a fresh backup and restore validation.
column13: The system must fail safely rather than report a successful backup with an invalid or incomplete recovery point.

column2: Stop only the backup execution container during a full backup
column4: Determine whether stopping only the container that performs the backup produces the same safe failure behavior as stopping the entire launcher pod.
column5: The compute container inside the virtual machine launcher pod
column6: Stop or signal the compute container
column10: The full backup should fail cleanly, the checkpoint should remain unchanged, and the VM should recover. The test also determines whether container-level disruption differs from pod-level disruption.
column12: Compare pod identity before and after, inspect the backup result and checkpoint, confirm Changed Block Tracking is enabled, then rerun backup and restore.
column13: Confirms that a failure at the actual backup execution process is handled consistently.

column2: Restart the backup controller when a full backup is starting
column4: Verify that the backup controller can fail over to its standby instance without creating duplicate backups or checkpoints.
column6: Delete the current controller leader pod
column7: After the backup request is accepted and is being reconciled, before the operation is complete
column8: Backup request is progressing and has no final result
column10: Leadership should move to the standby controller. Backup reconciliation should resume and the full backup should complete successfully without duplicate checkpoints.
column12: Confirm a new leader is elected, both controller replicas become ready, exactly one checkpoint is created, the tracker is updated once, and the backup can be restored.
column13: Demonstrates controller failover without duplicate or lost backup state.

column2: Restart the backup controller during the active disk copy
column4: Verify that a controller restart during the actual copy does not interrupt the data copy and that the new controller can complete reconciliation correctly.
column6: Delete the current controller leader pod
column7: While the full backup is actively copying data
column10: The disk copy should continue because it runs in the virtual machine launcher. The new controller should detect completion, clean up the temporary attachment, update the tracker, and mark the backup successful.
column12: Confirm leader failover, successful backup completion, one tracker update, cleanup of temporary volume attachment, and successful restore.
column13: Shows separation between the data-copy process and controller reconciliation.

column2: Restart the node backup handler during a full backup
column4: Verify behavior when the node-level virtualization handler responsible for backup state reporting is interrupted during an active full backup.
column5: Virtualization handler on the CBT worker node
column6: Delete the virtualization handler pod on the CBT node
column10: The system may either complete after the handler returns or fail with a clear backup-status-lost error. A successful-looking backup must never advance the checkpoint incorrectly.
column12: Confirm the handler returns, inspect the final backup result, verify the tracker is consistent, and run a clean follow-up backup.
column13: Confirms safe handling of node-level control-plane interruption.

column2: Restart storage access before the backup destination is attached
column4: Verify that temporary loss of the storage access component delays destination provisioning and hotplugging but recovers without corrupting the backup workflow.
column6: Delete the CSI node plugin pod
column7: After the backup starts but before the destination volume is bound and attached
column8: Backup is progressing and destination PVC is not yet bound
column10: Destination provisioning or hotplugging should pause while the CSI component restarts. Once storage access returns, the destination should bind, attach, and the backup should continue or fail cleanly if the delay exceeds controller tolerance.
column12: Confirm CSI recovery, destination PVC binding, successful volume attachment, final backup state, and tracker consistency.
column13: Shows whether the storage attachment path recovers cleanly from a transient outage.

column2: Restart storage access during an active full backup
column4: Determine whether an already-mounted backup destination remains usable when the storage access component is restarted during active writes.
column6: Delete the CSI node plugin pod
column10: The behavior is intentionally being established by the test. The copy may continue because the volume is already mounted, or it may fail cleanly. In either case, the system must not report invalid data as successful.
column12: Verify CSI recovery, PVC state, backup result, checkpoint state, backup image integrity, and restore result.
column13: Identifies the actual recovery behavior of active storage I/O after a CSI restart.

column2: Run out of space on the full backup destination
column4: Verify that the backup fails safely when the destination storage reaches capacity, without advancing the checkpoint or treating a partial backup as valid.
column6: Fill the destination PVC to approximately 95% capacity
column7: After the destination is bound and the backup has started, before the copy completes
column8: Backup is progressing and destination PVC is bound
column10: The backup should hit insufficient-space conditions and terminate as a clean failure. The VM should remain running and the tracker should not advance.
column11: Remove the filler or start a fresh run with a new destination PVC
column12: Check the failure reason, confirm tracker remains unchanged, verify the partial image is not considered valid, and confirm a fresh backup succeeds.
column13: Confirms safe handling of destination capacity exhaustion and prevents false-success backups.

column2: Create sustained storage I/O contention during a full backup
column4: Measure how the backup behaves when the underlying CBT storage filesystem is under sustained I/O pressure.
column5: CBT storage filesystem on the worker node
column6: Generate controlled I/O load on the CBT storage path
column10: The backup should take longer than the normal approximately 29-second baseline but should still complete successfully and produce correct data.
column12: Compare backup duration with the baseline, confirm successful completion and checkpoint advancement, and verify restored data matches the expected hash.
column13: Measures performance degradation while preserving backup correctness.

column2: Create CPU pressure during a full backup
column4: Measure the effect of node CPU pressure on backup completion and data correctness.
column5: CBT worker node hosting the VM
column6: Generate controlled CPU load on the node
column10: The backup may take longer and freeze/thaw may produce a warning, but the operation should complete with correct backup data.
column12: Confirm node and VM remain healthy, record duration and any warning, then validate the restored data.
column13: Measures resilience to compute contention without introducing uncontrolled VM failure.

column2: Block network traffic to the virtual machine during backup startup
column4: Verify that pod network isolation does not incorrectly interrupt the local backup data path or backup control mechanism.
column6: Apply an IP-level network filter to the launcher pod
column7: After the backup request starts but before the actual copy begins
column8: Backup is progressing but the copy has not started
column10: The backup is expected to continue because the backup copy and handler-to-launcher control path are node-local rather than dependent on pod IP traffic. The test validates this architectural isolation.
column12: Confirm the pod remains running, backup completes, tracker advances correctly, and restore validation succeeds.
column13: Confirms that the backup data path is independent of pod networking.

column2: Block controller access to the Kubernetes API during a full backup
column4: Verify that controller failover can recover from loss of API connectivity to the current controller leader without creating duplicate checkpoint state.
column5: Current backup controller leader network access
column6: Block API-server traffic from the controller leader
column7: While the backup is being reconciled
column10: The isolated leader should lose its lease and the standby controller should take over. The backup should complete with one checkpoint and no duplicate state.
column11: Network filter is removed; leader election settles
column12: Confirm new leader, both replicas ready, exactly one checkpoint, correct tracker update, successful restore, and successful subsequent incremental backup.
column13: Validates controller failover when the active leader temporarily loses API connectivity.

column2: Stop the controller during backup cleanup and checkpoint update
column4: Test the narrow transition window after the data copy finishes but before cleanup and checkpoint state updates are complete.
column6: Delete the controller leader during cleanup
column7: Immediately after the backup copy reports successful completion but before the backup becomes fully complete
column8: Backup copy completed but final status has not yet been recorded
column10: The new controller should complete volume cleanup and update the tracker exactly once. No orphaned temporary volume attachment or duplicate checkpoint should remain.
column12: Confirm no temporary hotplug pod remains, no stale utility volume remains, tracker advances exactly once, backup succeeds, and a subsequent incremental backup works.
column13: Tests one of the most sensitive state-transition points where a successful copy becomes a durable recovery point.

column2: Restart the virtual machine between full and incremental backups
column4: Exercise Changed Block Tracking checkpoint recovery after a VM restart and verify whether the next backup remains incremental or correctly falls back to a full backup.
column6: Delete the VMI after the full backup has completed and before the incremental backup begins
column7: After a successful full backup and before incremental backup creation
column8: Full backup checkpoint is recorded and no incremental backup exists
column10: The VM should restart. Changed Block Tracking should reinitialize and attempt checkpoint redefinition. The next backup should either remain genuinely incremental or follow the documented full-backup fallback. A silent incorrect incremental is a failure.
column11: Automatic VM restart and checkpoint recovery
column12: Record checkpoint-redefinition state, backup type, events, and restore data. Verify the actual resulting backup chain rather than assuming it is incremental.
column13: Validates the core CBT recovery mechanism after a VM lifecycle restart.

column2: Stop the virtual machine launcher during an incremental backup
column4: Verify that interrupting the actual incremental data copy does not advance the tracker to an invalid checkpoint and that the previous full recovery point remains usable.
column6: Delete the launcher pod
column7: During the active incremental disk-copy period
column10: The incremental backup should fail cleanly. The tracker must continue to reference the previous successful full checkpoint. The VM should restart and the incremental operation can be retried.
column11: Automatic VM restart followed by retry
column12: Confirm failure reason, unchanged full checkpoint, VM recovery, successful restoration of the original full backup, and successful retry.
column13: Confirms that an interrupted incremental cannot corrupt the checkpoint chain.

column2: Interrupt the controller during the incremental checkpoint update
column4: Verify that a controller restart around the checkpoint update does not leave the tracker in an incomplete or duplicated state.
column6: Delete the controller leader during the checkpoint-update gap
column7: After the full backup completes but before its checkpoint is visible to the incremental workflow
column8: Full backup succeeded but tracker update is delayed or incomplete
column10: The new controller should finish the tracker update. A harness timeout must be distinguished from an actual KubeVirt state-consistency failure.
column12: Measure failover time, confirm tracker eventually contains the correct checkpoint exactly once, then perform an incremental restore validation.
column13: Tests consistency of the handoff between backup completion and durable tracker state.

column2: Create storage I/O contention during an incremental backup
column4: Measure whether sustained storage contention slows an incremental backup while preserving its incremental nature and data correctness.
column5: CBT storage filesystem on the worker node
column6: Generate controlled I/O load on the CBT storage path
column10: The incremental backup should take longer than the normal approximately 15-second baseline but should still complete as an incremental backup with the correct changed data.
column12: Confirm backup type is incremental, checkpoint is distinct and correct, compare duration with baseline, and verify combined restore hash and marker.
column13: Measures incremental performance under storage contention while validating data correctness.

column2: Run out of space on the incremental backup destination
column4: Verify that incremental backup capacity exhaustion fails safely and leaves the previous full checkpoint and artifact usable.
column6: Fill the incremental destination PVC to approximately 95% capacity
column7: After incremental backup starts and its destination is bound
column10: The incremental backup should fail cleanly. The tracker must continue to reference the previous full checkpoint, and the full backup artifact must remain restorable.
column11: Use a fresh destination PVC and rerun
column12: Verify failure state, unchanged full checkpoint, valid full restore without the incremental marker, and successful retry.
column13: Confirms that storage exhaustion cannot invalidate the last known-good recovery point.

column2: Restart the node backup handler during an incremental backup
column4: Verify that interruption of the node-level backup handler during bitmap copying does not silently change an incremental backup into an incorrect full backup.
column5: Virtualization handler on the CBT worker node
column6: Delete the virtualization handler pod
column10: The incremental backup should recover or fail cleanly. Any resulting full backup must be explicitly explained by the checkpoint recovery behavior; an unexplained silent change from incremental to full is a finding.
column12: Record backup type, tracker state, checkpoint-redefinition state, events, and restore correctness.
column13: Specifically tests the integrity of the incremental checkpoint chain under handler interruption.

column2: Disable the guest agent before an incremental backup
column4: Verify the documented best-effort behavior when the guest agent cannot freeze and thaw the VM filesystem during backup.
column5: Guest qemu guest agent inside the VM
column6: Stop the guest agent from inside the VM, then run the incremental backup
column8: VM is ready and no backup is in progress
column10: The backup should complete with a warning rather than fail because freeze/thaw is best effort. The resulting backup should remain data-correct for the synchronized test data.
column12: Confirm guest-agent disconnected state, warning event, successful incremental result, combined restore hash, marker presence, and clean follow-up backup.
column13: Validates backup consistency behavior when application/filesystem quiescing is unavailable.

column2: Stop only the backup execution container during an incremental backup
column4: Verify container-level interruption during an incremental copy and compare it with complete launcher-pod interruption.
column5: Compute container inside the virtual machine launcher
column6: Stop or signal the compute container
column10: The incremental backup should fail cleanly and the tracker should remain on the previous valid checkpoint. VM recovery should restore the CBT state.
column12: Compare pod identity, backup result, tracker checkpoint, VM recovery, and retry restore validation.
column13: Confirms safe handling when only the actual backup execution process is interrupted.

column2: Stop restore verification while rebuilding the backup image
column4: Verify that interrupting the restore verification process does not alter the backup artifacts and that verification can be safely rerun.
column6: Delete the restore verification pod during conversion or rebase
column10: The verification should stop. Because backup PVCs are mounted read-only, the backup artifacts should remain unchanged.
column12: Confirm backup PVCs remain bound and unchanged, then rerun verification and compare hashes and marker semantics with the baseline.
column13: Shows that restore validation is isolated from backup artifact integrity.

column2: Create storage I/O contention during restore verification
column4: Measure how storage contention affects offline restore conversion without changing the stored backup artifacts.
column5: CBT storage filesystem on the worker node
column6: Generate controlled I/O load on the CBT storage path
column7: While restore verification is converting or rebasing the images
column10: Restore processing should slow down but complete within the existing verification timeout and produce the same hashes and marker results.
column12: Confirm restore succeeds, compare full and combined hashes with baseline, verify marker semantics, and confirm backup artifacts are unchanged.
column13: Measures restore performance under storage contention while protecting data correctness.

column2: Restart storage access before restore volumes are mounted
column4: Verify that restore verification recovers when storage access is interrupted before its read-only backup volumes are mounted.
column6: Delete the CSI node plugin pod before restore volumes are mounted
column7: After restore verification pod is created but before it starts using the PVCs
column8: Restore pod is pending waiting for volume access
column10: The restore pod should remain pending while storage access is unavailable and should recover after the CSI plugin returns. If it cannot recover, it should fail cleanly without modifying artifacts.
column12: Confirm CSI recovery, backup PVCs remain unchanged, restore pod eventually succeeds or fails cleanly, and rerun produces identical hashes.
column13: Validates restore startup behavior during a transient storage-access outage.

column2: Apply bounded memory pressure during backup
column4: Measure backup behavior under controlled memory pressure while ensuring the pressure is low enough to avoid intentionally killing the VM.
column5: CBT worker node hosting the VM
column6: Generate bounded memory pressure on the node
column10: Backup may slow down. The launcher VM must not be unintentionally OOM-killed; if it is, the result becomes equivalent to a launcher failure and must be classified separately.
column12: Check for OOM kills, backup result, tracker consistency, restored data, and clean follow-up run.
column13: Measures resource pressure while separating graceful degradation from uncontrolled VM termination.

column2: Restart the worker node kubelet during a full backup
column4: Verify that restarting kubelet temporarily affects node management and status reporting without unnecessarily restarting the running VM or interrupting the backup.
column5: Kubelet on the CBT worker node
column6: Restart kubelet on the worker node
column10: The running VM and backup should continue. Pod status reporting may pause and then recover. The test must first validate the scenario in dry-run mode because the environment is bare metal.
column12: Confirm node returns Ready, launcher pod identity and restart count remain unchanged, backup succeeds, tracker advances once, and restore validation passes.
column13: Validates node-management recovery without intentionally disrupting the VM workload.

column2: Block all network traffic to the virtual machine during the backup copy
column4: Confirm that blocking IP traffic to the launcher does not interrupt the node-local backup copy and identify the effect on guest access used by the test harness.
column6: Block all IP traffic to the launcher pod
column10: The backup copy is expected to continue. Guest SSH used by the test harness may stop working temporarily, but this should not affect the local backup data path.
column12: Confirm launcher remains running, backup succeeds, tracker advances, restore data is correct, and guest access recovers.
column13: Demonstrates that backup data movement is independent of pod networking.

column2: Combine storage contention with launcher failure during backup
column4: Test a combined failure in which storage is under pressure and the backup execution process is then stopped, verifying that the system still fails cleanly and recovers end-to-end.
column5: Virtual machine launcher plus CBT storage filesystem
column6: Start controlled storage I/O pressure, then stop the launcher during the same active backup
column9: 90 seconds of I/O load; launcher stopped approximately 20 seconds after load begins
column10: The backup should fail cleanly without advancing the tracker. The VM should recover. A complete clean full and incremental backup/restore cycle should work afterward.
column11: Automatic VM recovery and storage load ends
column12: Verify node and VM recovery, failure reason, unchanged tracker after the failed backup, then run a complete clean full and incremental workflow with hash and marker validation.
column13: End-to-end combined test for the hardest-to-attribute failure condition; should be run last.
